itinerary.title: Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut
itinerary.description:
After having your breakfast we will make a short journey from the hotel to Marangu National Park gate for the necessary formalities at the gate. We start the climbs through fascinating tropical rain forest; we reach the first hut at Mandara for dinner and overnight. An alternative is to simply rest and relax the beautiful forest around the camp. Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut (2,700 m)
Walking hours: 5-6 hours walking.
Zone: Rainforest.

itinerary.title: Mandara hut to Horombo hut
itinerary.description:
The first part of the walk is a steep ascent through forest, but the path soon opens out into moorland and in clear weather, there are great views of Kibo and Mawenzi peaks. We arrive at Horombo Hut mid-afternoon, where you can relax and enjoy the stunning scenery around the camp. Mandara Hut to Horombo Hut (3,720 m)
Walking hours: 4-6 hours walking.
Zone: Low Alpine Zone.

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut to Kibo hut
itinerary.description:
We climb very gradually towards the lunar desert of the Saddle between Mawenzi and Kibo.
These 6-7 hours walking will be taken at a slow pace until we reach Kibo Hut (4,700m), where we will spend the night in a comfortable hut.
There is no running water at Kibo Hut. The remainder of the day is spent relaxing in preparation for the final ascent before a very early night. Horombo Hut to Kibo Hut (4,700 meters) 4-6 hours walking.

itinerary.title: Kibo Hut to Summit to Horrombo Hut
itinerary.description:
Wake up before midnight in the cover of darkness. We begin a steep climb over loose volcanic screed has some well-graded zig-zags and a slow but steady pace will take us to rim of the main crater, Gillman’s 5,685 m.
We will rest there for few minutes to enjoy the sunrise over Mawenzi. Those who are still feeling good can continue slowly to make the three hour round trip from here along the crater rim to Uhuru peak 5,895 m. which is the highest point in Africa.
After a few minutes to appreciate your accomplishment we descend to Kibo Hut is amazingly fast.

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut

itinerary.title: Full day in Serengeti National Park Game Drive
itinerary.description: After breakfast 7:00am you will start exploring Serengeti. The Serengeti National Park is the jewel in the crown of Tanzania’s game parks and offers arguably the best game viewing in Africa. The setting is perfect – a sea of endless plains that stretches to the horizon, dotted with the occasional acacia tree and termite mound. This Savannah is home to huge herds of buffalo that every year make the mass migration north, through crocodile infested rivers, in a frenzied mixture of mating and galloping that is driven by instinct. Prides of lion rule here, their hungry gaze sweeping the Savannah for a chance to attack the thousands of elands, impala and gazelle. Solitary leopard stakes out their place in the high branches of the acacia tree and herds of elephant’s roam at will. This is Africa that you have always dreamed about. You will have your picnic lunch and Later in the afternoon you will leave Serengeti to Ngorongoro for Dinner and overnight at Tented Lodge in Ngorongoro

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater Game Drive to Karatu
itinerary.description: After breakfast 08:00am, we will start our journey to Ngorongoro Crater. We will descend 600 meters down Ngorongoro conservation area for the game drive. This magnificent crater is one of the most densely crowded African wildlife areas in the world and is home to an estimated 30,000 animals including some of Tanzania’s last remaining Black Rhino. Supported by a year-round water supply and fodder, the Ngorongoro crater support a vast variety of animals, which include herds of Wildebeest, Zebra, Buffalo, Eland, Warthog, Hippo, and giant African Elephants. Another uniqueness of the crater is its huge population of predators, which include Lions, Hyenas, Jackals, Cheetahs and the ever-elusive Leopard. In the afternoon, you will enjoy your picnic lunch at the Hippo pool. You will continue with afternoon game drive, then you will ascend to the top of the crater then transfer to Karatu.  Dinner and Overnight at Eileens Tree Inn Karatu.

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara National park and Mto wa Mbu cultural tour
itinerary.description: After breakfast at Karatu, you will start driving to Lake Manyara National Park about 30min from Karatu Town. While the scenic beauty of this park certainly makes it worth a visit, the game viewing here is not as rewarding as in Tanzania's other Northern parks.  Nonetheless, famous for its tree-climbing lions, flamingos, large concentration of elephants, buffalo and monkeys, as well as breath-taking scenery and soda-ash lake in the centre, Manyara should definitely not be missed!  You will start game drive till noon then proceed to  Mto wa mbu a village adjacent to the park for hot traditional lunch.  Your guide will be from the village itself so you will have a unique opportunity to see the community through his eyes. Tours last around 2 hours, but are flexible. During your visit you’ll get a good feel for the social side of the village – the farms and the milling machines, the schools, markets and churches. You’ll likely start in the village banana plantation, where they grow different varieties of bananas. Then you on the way you will visit milling machines, schools and a church. Next you might visit a youth art project, and learn about the different painting styles and techniques. The artists are happy for you to ask questions and take photos. Your tour will finish in the bustling local market, where you can wander around stalls selling fruit and vegetables stalls, spices and meals. After your tour you will proceed to Arusha   and arrive before 5pm: If you will travel the same day our driver guide will drop you at the Airport

itinerary.title: Visit Lake Manyara
itinerary.description: After breakfast, you will be picked up from your Hotel and then drive to Lake Manyara National Park for game drive, late afternoon drive to Hotel for dinner and overnight. Lake Manyara. The name Manyara is derived from the Masai word “Emanyara”, which is a Euphorbia species of plant that is found around a family homestead in the area. After an early breakfast we drive down into the valley and explore the Lake Manyara National Park. Stretching for 50km along the base of the rusty-gold 600-metre high Rift Valley escarpment. Here guests will be introduced to large buffalo, wildebeest, giraffes and zebra herds congregating on the grassy plains while the narrow belt of acacia wood bordering the plains are the favored haunt of Manyara’s legendary tree-climbing lions and impressively tusked elephants. Taking in the expansive views eastward, across the central soda lake we will be amazed by the sight of thousands of pink-hued flamingos on their perpetual migration, as well as other large water birds such as storks, cormorants and pelicans. At the Southern end of the park we will visit algae-streaked sulphur hot water springs known as (MajiMoto) bubbling from deep within the earth.

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara-Serengeti
itinerary.description: After breakfast we continue with the game drive to the world famous Serengeti National Park which derives its name from the Masai for “endless plain”, is the jewel of Tanzania’s protected areas and lies on a vast plateau between the eastern arm of the Rift Valley and the huge expanse of Lake Victoria. Tanzania’s oldest and most popular national park and a World Heritage site, the Serengeti is best known for the annual migration of hundreds of thousands of wildebeest, zebra and Thomson’s gazelle. Spectacular game viewing—of buffalo, elephant, giraffe, topi, impala, Grant’s gazelle, lion and leopard is a highlight. Be inspired by the “amazing Acadia trees” dotted throughout the Serengeti, where visitors are treated with some of the most mesmerizing sunsets in the world. Our small safari vehicles minimize drive times and improve your chances of snapping that perfect shot of one of the elusive ‘Big 5’

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater - Arusha
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, you will drive for approximately 30 minutes to the crater floor.
Upon arrival, you will be amazed by the concentration and sheer number and diversity of animals and bird life! Seated or standing in your safari vehicle, the game viewing opportunities will be endless...
The Ngorongoro Crater is a breathtakingly beautiful setting and the best place in East Africa to see the Big Five. On the crater floor you can expect to see herds of zebra, wildebeest, Thomson’s gazelle, Grant’s gazelle, topi and many more. Sightings of predators such as lion, hyena, jackal and bat-eared fox regularly occur here as well. Although cheetah and leopard are a little more scarce in this park, they can still be spotted with a little luck.  Ngorongoro Crater is also one of a handful of places in Africa where you have a very good chance of seeing rhino, though usually from a distance. Bird species are also numerous and varied here.
After your half-day safari in the crater, we will leave the park and head back to town. You will be dropped off at your hotel in Arusha or Moshi in the evening, or even at Kilimanjaro International Airport depending on what you have planned for the remainder of your stay in Tanzania.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro to Serengeti National Park

The setting is perfect – a sea of endless plains that stretches to the horizon, dotted with the occasional acacia tree and termite mound. This Savannah is home to huge herds of buffalo that every year make the mass migration north during August/September, through crocodile infested rivers, in a frenzied mixture of mating and galloping that is driven by instinct. Prides of lion rule here, their hungry gaze sweeping the Savannah for a chance to attack the thousands of elands, impala and gazelle. Solitary leopard stakes out their place in the high branches of the acacia tree and herds of elephant’s roam at will. This is Africa that you have always dreamed about. Among other places, you will visit the Datoga pastoralists and members of the Hadzabe tribe. The Hadzabe are one of two remaining hunter-gatherer tribes in Tanzania. There are approximately 1500 families left in this tribe. Lake Eyasi offers excellent views of the Rift Valley escarpment and is an ideal destination for relaxing and bird-watching. After activities you will have your lunch and later in the afternoon, drive to Karatu. Dinner and Accommodation at Marera Valley Lodge/ Eileens Tree Inn (full board)

After lunch, you will proceed to Mto wa mbu a village adjacent to the park.  Your guide will be from the village itself so you will have a unique opportunity to see the community through his eyes. Tours last around 2 hours, but are flexible. During your visit you’ll get a good feel for the social side of the village – the farms and the milling machines, the schools, markets and churches. You’ll likely start in the village banana plantation, where they grow different varieties of bananas. Then you on the way you will visit milling machines, schools and a church. Next you might visit a youth art project, and learn about the different painting styles and techniques. The artists are happy for you to ask questions and take photos. Your tour will finish in the bustling local market, where you can wander around stalls selling fruit and vegetables stalls, spices and meal. After your tour you will proceed to Moshi for an overnight at Park View Inn/ Panama Garden Resort (Bed and Breakfast)

itinerary.title: Materuni Waterfalls and Coffee Tour in Moshi
itinerary.description: You will leave the hotel 8:00 am after breakfast to Materuni Waterfalls and Coffee Tour. Materuni Waterfall is the highest and most impressive waterfall at the foothill of Mt. Kilimanjaro. You’ll visit a coffee farm and learn about how coffee is grown, harvested and processed, and you’ll try your hand at roasting and preparing a fresh cup of coffee the Chagga way. After coffee tour and test you’ll take a beautiful 30 minutes hike through the hills and valleys en route to the Materuni. The valleys and hills are covered by tropical rainforest, coffee, banana and avocado “shambas”, the Kiswahili word for farms. On a clear day great view of Kibo and Moshi town can be seen during hiking. The hike to the base of the Waterfall can be demanding and hiking boots are recommended. Finally, you can refresh at the waterfall’s cold water, so don’t forget to bring your swim wear. Later you will leave back to Moshi town at 1pm. Later return to Moshi Accommodation at Park View Inn/ Panama Garden Resort (Bed and Breakfast)

itinerary.description:
Pick up at Arusha Airport and transfer to Tarangire National Park for Game Drive. You will drive for approximately 2.5 hrs to Tarangire National Park. As we zip along we pass many Maasai in their colorful dress walking on the roadside, riding bicycles, herding cattle and driving donkey’s carts. Tarangire is a lovely, quiet park in Northern Tanzania. It is most famous for its elephant migration, birding and authentic safari atmosphere.
 Every year during the dry season from June to November, the wildlife migrate through the park allowing for a very large number of different species to be seen here. As most of this part of the country is dry, the Tarangire River remains the only source of water and consequently attracts large numbers of wildebeests, elephants, gazelles, zebras, hartebeest, buffaloes and various predators such as lions and cheetahs that come to drink and graze around the river banks. Large swathes of Tarangire remain almost untouched, especially in the southern region of the park.  With game-viewing that is exceptional in the dry season, this Tanzanian safari park is a small gem on the Northern safari circuit, especially if you love elephants! After game drive you will drive to Maramboi Tented Lodge (full Board).

On our exploration of the park we will see monkey, giraffe, zebra, wildebeest, buffalo, elephant, and, with some luck, lions lounging in the trees. The park is known for its diverse landscapes; not only open grassy plains but also primate-filled woodlands and baobab dotted cliffs. title: 6-Days Zanzibar Beach Experience
overview:
Description of the tour

Zanzibar is an archipelago off the coast of East Africa, part of the United Republic of Tanzania, known for its idyllic beaches, rich history, and vibrant cultural mixes. It consists primarily of two main islands which are Unguja often simply referred to as “Zanzibar” and Pemba as well as numerous smaller islands. Unguja, the largest island, is where Zanzibar City and the historic Stone Town are located. A six-day tour to Zanzibar is a fantastic way to experience the island’s stunning beaches, rich cultural heritage, and unique natural beauty. Zanzibar captures the best of the island’s history, culture, and natural beauty, offering a blend of relaxation and exploration in one of the Indian Ocean’s most breathtaking destinations.

Highlights of the tour

  • Stone town city exploration
  • Prison island visit
  • Spice farm experience
  • Beach experience
  • Mnemba snorkelling
  • Kwale island

itinerary.title: stone town city exploration
itinerary.description: Stone Town the historic heart of Zanzibar City, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its rich blend of African, Arab, Indian, and European cultural influences. Located on the western coast of Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago, Stone Town offers a unique fusion of architecture, history, and vibrant cultural life that reflects its centuries-old role as a major trade centre in the Indian Ocean. Our guide will meet you at the starting point the Anglican Cathedral. After introduction, our tour will start by visiting the former Slave Market, the Anglican Cathedral, the House of Wonders, the Sultan’s Palace Museum and Old Arab. You’ll explore also the local markets and see seafood and fish piled high, fresh loaves of bread in wicker baskets and stacks of fruit and vegetables, as traders sell their goods from market stalls. The tour will also include visits to the Freddie Mercury house, Zanzibar Curio Shop, Jaws Corner coffee shop and many important destinations in stone town. The tour will be very flexible based on what you would-like to see in stone town. Later in the evening the guide will drop you off in the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Kwale island exploration
itinerary.description: Kwale Island, located off the southern coast of Zanzibar, Tanzania, is a hidden gem known for its stunning natural beauty and tranquil atmosphere. This small island is part of the larger Kwale Archipelago and is often less crowded than some of the more popular tourist destinations in Zanzibar, making it an ideal spot for those seeking a peaceful getaway. It is also known as blue safari trip where by our guide in the morning will pick you up heading to Kwale island by boat for half day to experience the beauty of this hidden gem. You will spend the time in that quite place to experience the magic of that blue safari trip. In the afternoon you will enjoy the most stunning sea food with fresh fruits then, after finish the day you will start a journey back to your hotel for relaxing, dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Prison island exploration
itinerary.description: Prison island Is a small, picturesque island located about 5.6 kilometres (3.5 miles) northwest of Stone Town, Zanzibar. This coral island is a popular tourist destination, known for its intriguing history, stunning beaches, and its sanctuary of giant Aldabra tortoises. You will have an opportunity to explore the rich culture and history of Zanzibar with a visit to Prison Island by boat. See the large tortoises that inhabit the Island, and enjoy the opportunity to snorkel off the coast. You will visit Prison Island on a private 3-hour tour, and discover the rich history and beautiful natural surroundings of this location. Meet your guide in Zanzibar, or select the option including hotel pickup, then enjoy the ride to the island on a traditional dhow. Learn how this small island gained its name and explore the place that is now home to more than 50 tortoises, some over 100 years old. You will also have another experience of feeding the tortoises and take up-close pictures with them, as you keep a lookout for the peacocks and antelope that also live there. After discovering the island and its history, take the opportunity to snorkel in the clear waters off the coast amongst tropical fish and colourful coral. At the end of your tour, you will return to Stone town, where you’ll be dropped off in the city centre, or at your hotel.

itinerary.title: Mnemba Atoll snorkelling
itinerary.description: Mnemba Atoll, located off the northeastern coast of Zanzibar, Tanzania, is renowned for its stunning snorkelling experiences. This small, private island is surrounded by crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral reefs, making it a popular destination for snorkelers and divers alike. The waters around Mnemba Atoll are teeming with marine life. Snorkelers can expect to see a variety of colourful fish, including parrotfish, clownfish, and angelfish, as well as sea turtles, dolphins, and even the occasional reef shark. In the morning after breakfast your guide will pick you up heading to Mnemba Atoll where you will spend the day to dive and snorkel in that beautiful Atoll. At noon the lunch will be provided where you will enjoy the most stunning sea food and fresh fruits or juice. Later in the evening you will jump in the boat heading to your accommodation center for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Spice farm tour and airport transfer
itinerary.description: After having a strong breakfast, you guide will pick you up to start a tour heading to spice farm. itinerary.title: Moshi/Arusha to Momella Gate to Miriakamba Hut
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:4-5 hours
Total Distance:8 km
Starting Altitude:2956m (9698ft)
Final Altitude:3978m (13054ft)
Environment: Lower heather zone
After breakfast 8:00am we will start our journey to and we drive to Momella Gate where we complete registration formalities and a national park ranger is assigned to accompany our group.
Setting off from Momella Gate, we take the southern route known for its abundant wildlife. The track passes through open grassland where there is the possibility of spotting buffalo grazing in one of the clearings. The fortunate few may see giraffe and elephants.
The forest section is especially scenic with strangler figs, wild mango, African olive and wild elder. Birdlife is abundant with common sightings of Hartlaub’s turaco, olive pigeon, white fronted bee eaters, fiscal shrike, stone chat, variable sunbirds and the tropical boubou. Trekkers with a keen eye will spot several species of butterflies such as the blue swallow-tail, soldier commodore, mocker swallow-tail, golden winged forester, emperor and forest mother of pearl.
We cross the Ngare Nanyuki river just above the Maio Waterfalls climbing steadily through lush montane forest until we reach the “Fig Tree” (famous for the roadway passing through it) where we enjoy our well-deserved lunch.
After lunch, the canopy begins to thin and we encounter many forms of bird life and hear the grunting calls of the magnificent black colobus monkeys with their long ‘cape’ of white hair and a flowing white tail.
Around 2300m the higher montane forest begins and is home to juniper and podo trees while beautiful wild flowers such as the empetient species, red-hot poker, orchids, fire ball lily and gladiolus adorn the trail.
By mid-afternoon the path clears and we encounter the first close views of the towering cliffs of Mt Meru and the stunning ash cone. Miriakampa Hut, situated in idyllic grassy glade, is reached in time to enjoy the afternoon sun and beautiful views over the surrounding plains towards Kilimanjaro.
From here we can go on an evening game walk in hopes of watching some wildlife at one of the watering holes in the crater.

itinerary.title: Miriakamba Hut to Saddle Hut
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:2-3 hours
Hiking Distance:4 km
Starting Altitude:2516m
Final Altitude:3570m
Environment: Heath
The track from Miriakampa Hut to the saddle below Little Meru is a steep sustained trek that tests your legs. Our track takes us through beautiful and lush montane forest and striking tree species such as hygenium abyssinica, nuxia congesta, podocarpus, and hypericum tevolutum with mosses and lichens adorning the ground and trees.
Passing the halfway point of Mgongo wa Tembo (Elephant Back Ridge) we pass through giant heather and moorland vegetation, home to common shrubs such as erica arbores, stoebe kilimandscharica and leonits nepatifolia.
Around midday we reach the alpine zone of Saddle Hut where we rest, set up our bunks and enjoy a picnic lunch.
In the afternoon, trekkers feeling energetic can make the short climb to the nearby summit of Little Meru (3820 m/ 12,533 ft) for superb views of Socialist Peak and the steep winding trail that awaits us the next morning. The round trip ascent of Little Meru takes 1-1.5 hours.
At these higher altitudes we encounter magnificent birdlife including the bearded vulture soaring high above us, white- naked raven, lammerger, stonechat, alpine swift and cliff chat found around camp.

itinerary.title: Saddle Hut to Summit to Miriakamba Hut
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:4-5 hours ascent + 6-8 hours descent
Hiking Distance:5 km ascent + 15 km descent
Starting Altitude:2516m
Summit:4566m
Final Altitude:2516m
Environment: Alpine Desert
At around 3am we rise, put on all our warm clothes and enjoy a hot cup of tea or chocolate before setting out
on the trail. The first hour is a steep climb to Rhino Point (3800m/12,467ft), and then the path continues along a narrow but spectacular ridge of ash and rock to reach Cobra Point (4350m/14,272ft).
The summit is now within our reach and after an hour of climbing and light scrambling over rocks and boulder we look up to see the summit flag beckoning us on wards and upwards.
Arriving at the summit we are greeted with stunning views of the crater rim, the spectacular ash cone rising from the crater floor, Kilimanjaro floating on the morning clouds just 70km away, and the Rift Valley in the distance.
After soaking up the magnificent vistas and celebrating our summit success we begin our descent where we may encounter the delicately-hoofed klipspringers bounding from rock to rock in the early morning light. The route back to Rhino Point in the sharp morning light traverses a narrow ridge between the sloping outer wall of the crater and the sheer cliffs of the inner wall is one of the most dramatic and exhilarating walks in Africa.
Arriving at Saddle Hut mid morning, we enjoy a sumptuous brunch before retracing our steps to Miriakamba Hut for Lunch, diner and overnight.

itinerary.title: Miriakamba Hut to Momella Gate-Arusha
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:2-3 hrs. trekking
Starting Altitude:2516m
Final Altitude:1500m
Environment: Moorland, Parkland
 After a leisurely morning we complete our 2-3 hour descent taking the direct route through open grassland and mixed forest, with good chances of seeing wildlife. The northern trail has excellent views back towards the crater, Momella Lakes and over the plains of the national park.
By late morning we reach Momella Gate and receive our summit certificates, say farewell to our crew and have time for a short picnic lunch and game drive before returning to Moshi or Arusha for some well-deserved shower and fresh clothes.

title: Kilimanjaro 7 Days Machame Route
overview: Kilimanjaro 7 days Machame route is highly recommended for high altitude acclimatization.The route is very scenic, providing hikers with incredible views and varying landscapes. Though the climbing can be done in six days/five nights for experienced climbers, the summit success rate is significantly higher when taking the 7-day option as it will allow you sufficient time to acclimate to the altitude. The route’s length is approximately 62 km/ 37 miles from start to finish (Machame Gate to Mweka Gate). According to statistics from Kilimanjaro National Park, approximately 50% of trekkers use the Machame Route to ascend Kilimanjaro. It is designed for physically fit people with some hiking experience, though plenty of first-time trekkers have taken Machame Route and done just fine.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Tanzania and transfer to the hotel
itinerary.description: Upon arrival in Tanzania via Kilimanjaro International airport (JRO), you will be picked up by a KLM Safaris staff member a KLM Safaris placard and transferred to Moshi town where you will spend your first night at a hotel.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Machame Gate
itinerary.description:
Transfer from your hotel to Machame Gate (1,640 meters or 5,380 ft) and climb to Machame Camp/Machame hut (2,850 meters or 9,350 ft)
Hiking hours: 5-6 hours.
Distance: 11 km or 7 miles.
Zone: Rainforest
After breakfast at your hotel our driver will pick you up and take you to Kilimanjaro National Park's Machame Gate (approximately 1 hour drive).
Upon arrival, our experienced and loyal porters will organize all the baggage and other equipment for the climb, while you and your guides register with Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA).
After all registration and other formalities are complete, you will start your trek through the dense mountain forest. There is a strong possibility of rain in the forest which means that the trail in this zone may become muddy and slippery. Proper hiking shoes and rainwear are a must! In this area you should also be on the lookout for wildlife such as Colobus monkeys and many species of birds.
You will stop for a picnic lunch at the halfway point before continuing on to Machame Camp where you will arrive in the late afternoon or early evening. The porters and cook who move up the mountain very fast, will set up your tents at the camp, boil your drinking water and prepare snacks for your arrival. You may get your first closer look at the glaciated dome of Kibo if the weather is clear and the clouds have dissipated. Your hot dinner will be served after some rest and washing up time at the camp.

itinerary.title: Climbing from Machame Camp to Shira Camp 2
itinerary.description:
Climbing from Machame Camp to Shira Camp 2 (3,810 meters or 12,500 feet)
Hiking hours: 5-6 hours.
Distance: 5 km or 3 miles.
Zone: Low Alpine Zone
After breakfast, a short hiking day will begin. You will be leaving the rain forest and entering a moorland area where you will be climbing up a steep ridge to reach a small semi-circular cliff known as picnic rock. There are excellent views of Kibo and the jagged rim of Shira plateau from here, and its also a good spot for a short rest. You will continue on your journey across many streams, as well as a rocky ridge onto Shira plateau that will then lead to Shira 2 Camp where you will stop for the night.
Our porters will have already set up your tents prior to your arrival at the camp and they will have prepared drinking and washing water for you. You will enjoy some evening snacks as well as a hot dinner prepared by your experienced mountain cook.
Be prepared for a cold night as temperatures can drop below freezing at the camp, although temperatures depend highly on seasonality.

itinerary.title: Climbing from Shira Camp 2 Via Lava Tower
itinerary.description:
Climbing from Shira Camp 2 Via Lava Tower (4,630 m 15, 190 ft) to Barranco Camp (3,976 meters or 13,044 feet)
Hiking hours: 8- 9 hours.
Distance: 10 km or 6 miles.
Zone: Low alpine zone to high alpine zone.
After breakfast, you will start a gentle ascent with panoramic views, leaving the moorland plateau behind you and entering into a semi-desert and rocky landscape.
After 5 hours of walking eastward, you will come face to face with the lava tower. Here you will have a chance to rest and eat your lunch. After, you will descend to the Great Barranco Valley, sheltered by towering cliffs and with extensive views of the plains far below. This trekking day is mainly to allow for acclimatization.
Drinking and washing water will be made  available upon your arrival at the camp and your hot dinner will be served after sunset.

itinerary.title: Climbing from Barranco Camp to Karanga Valley Camp
itinerary.description:
Climbing from Barranco Camp to Karanga Valley Camp (3,995 meters or 13,106 feet)
Hiking hours: 4- 5 hours.
Distance: 4 km or 2 miles.
Zone: High alpine zone
After your night at Great Barranco Camp and a hearty breakfast, you will begin your climb up the eastern wall of the gorge while admiring the spectacular view of Kilimanjaro’s ice fields and frost-covered landscape.
You will then climb up the magnificent Barranco wall, also known as the breakfast wall, after which you will continue along a calm trail until you reach the Karanga Valley Camp. Here you will settle in and mentally prepare for the next stretch of your journey. A hot dinner will be served after sunset.

itinerary.title: Climbing from Karanga Valley Camp to Barafu Camp
itinerary.description:
Climbing from Karanga Valley Camp to Barafu Camp (4.673 meters to 15,331 feet)
Hiking hours: 4 hours.
Distance: 4 km or 2 miles.
Zone: High alpine zone
After breakfast, you will embark on your last day full day on the Kilimanjaro Machame Route before reaching the summit. You will cross some splendid volcanic lands, with Kibo volcano (highest of the Kilimanjaro volcanoes) and its remaining glaciers as the backdrop. Your tents will be exposed to freezing winds and the campsite is set among many rocks. Your guide will brief you on how to prepare for your summit night. Also, make sure you settle down to rest and sleep by 7:00 PM so as to feel fit and well for your nighttime ascension. Your dinner will be served earlier than usual on this important day.

itinerary.title: Climbing to Uhuru Peak
itinerary.description:
Climbing to Uhuru Peak (5,895 meters or 19,341feet) and descend to Mweka Camp (10,000ft)
Hiking hours: 4-6 hours.Distance 12 km or 7 Miles.
Zone: Glacial zone and the all preceding zones.
Your guide will wake you up at around 11:30pm for tea and biscuits before you begin your summit attempt. The route heads northwest and you will ascend over large rocks and stone scree. During the ascent, many hikers feel that this is the most mentally and physically challenging part of the climb.
After about 6 hours, you will reach Stella Point (5685m), located on the crater rim. After enjoying the magnificent sunrise, you will continue ascending for about 2 hours on a snow-covered trail to Uhuru Peak (5895m). Reaching the summit of Mt. Kilimanjaro is a lifetime accomplishment! Once you are there, you will be able to spend a short time on the summit taking photographs before the descent to Barafu Camp begins.
Once back at Barafu camp, you will rest and enjoy a hot lunch in the sun. After eating, you will continue descending down to Mweka Hut. The Mweka Trail will lead you through the scree and rocks to the moorland and eventually into the rain forest. Mweka Camp is located in the upper rain forest so fog and rain should be expected.
Here, you will be served a well-deserved hot dinner and be able to wash and rest after your feet.

itinerary.title: Descend from Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate
itinerary.description:
Descent from Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate (1,640 meters or 5,340 feet)
Hiking hours: 3 – 4 hours
Distance: 10 km or 6 miles
Zone: Rainforest
Following a well-deserved breakfast, your staff will have a big party full of singing and dancing to celebrate your ascension of Mount Kilimanjaro. It is at this time that you can present your tips to your guide, assistant guides, chef(s) and porters.
Following the celebration, you will begin your descent from Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate where TANAPA requires all hikers to sign the register. You will also receive a certificate of completion at this time. Hikers who reached Stella Point (5685m) receive green certificates and hikers who reached Uhuru Peak (5895m) receive gold certificates.
Once all the formalities are completed you will be transferred back to your hotel in Moshi.

This section is very steep with a lot of stone scree, requiring a great physical and mental effort, probably the most demanding section of the entire route. From Gillman’s Point you will normally encounter snow all the way up to Uhuru peak (5895m), the highest point in Africa. Total exhilaration and satisfaction set in – you made it! Weather conditions on the summit will determine how long you can spend taking photographs before the descent back to Kibo hut. Once there, you will have a short rest then begin your descent to Horombo hut where you will overnight.

title: Kilimanjaro 6 Days Umbwe Route
overview: The Umbwe Route is widely regarded as the hardest trail, a tough vertical slog through the jungle, in places using the tree roots as makeshift rungs on a ladder. Having reached the Southern Circular Route, trekkers can continue Northwest to tackle Kibo from the West and the difficult Arrow Glacier Route; or you can follow the Southern Circular Route east around to Barafu and approach the summit from there. The entire walk up and down takes a minimum of five days.

The first day is through the Montana Forest. Lush vegetation with old trees and lilts of ferns and mosses mark this area that gets reliable rain year round. The forest abounds with wildlife, small bushbucks and duikers as well as monkeys. There is also a rich and varied bird-life. The first 3 hours or so is on a gently rising land before steepening for the last 2 hours. The camp for the night is in a small clearing on the trail.

The ridge narrows and sharpens, finally becoming like a knife-edge with steep drops on each side. As the height of the vegetation decreases there are stunning views of both Kilimanjaro’s southern flank and across Mount Meru some 50 miles away.

The rest of the day is spent skirting the base of Kibo Peak over left shoulder. We descend down into the Karanga Valley, where we rest up for the night before the tough climb up Barafu hut.

We walk very slowly in the darkness on a switchback trail through large boulders and loose volcanic scree to reach the crater rim at Gillman’s Point (5,685 meters). We rest here for a short time to enjoy the spectacular sunrise over Mawenzi. Those who are still feeling strong can make the three-hour round trip to Uhuru Peak (5895 meters), passing close to the spectacular glaciers and ice cliffs that still occupy most of the summit area. The descent to Kibo Hut  is surprisingly fast and, after some refreshments, we continue the descent to Horombo Huts).

itinerary.title: Arusha to Momella Gate to Miriakamba Hut
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:4-5 hours (Drive 1 hour)
Hiking Distance:10 km
Starting Altitude:1500m
Final Altitude:2516m
Environment: Parkland/Montane Forest
Trekkers arrange their own accommodation and we meet in Arusha after breakfast. We drive to Momella Gate where we complete registration formalities and a national park ranger is assigned to accompany our group.
Setting off from Momella Gate, we take the southern route known for its abundant wildlife. The track passes through open grassland where there is the possibility of spotting buffalo grazing in one of the clearings. The fortunate few may see giraffe and elephants.
The forest section is especially scenic with fig trees, wild mango, African olive and wild elder. Birdlife is abundant with common sightings of Hartlaub’s turaco, olive pigeon, white fronted bee eaters, fiscal shrike, stone chat, variable sunbirds and the tropical boubou. Trekkers with a keen eye will spot several species of butterflies such as the blue swallow-tail, soldier commodore, mocker swallow-tail, golden winged forester, emperor and forest mother of pearl.
We cross the Ngare Nanyuki river just above the Maio Waterfalls climbing steadily through lush montane forest until we reach the “Fig Tree” (famous for the roadway passing through it) where we enjoy our well deserved lunch.
After lunch, the canopy begins to thin and we encounter many forms of bird life and hear the grunting calls of the magnificent black colobus monkeys with their long ‘cape’ of white hair and a flowing white tail.
Around 2300m the higher montane forest begins and is home to juniper and podo trees while beautiful wild flowers such as the empetient species, red-hot poker, orchids, fire ball lily and gladiolus adorn the trail.
By mid-afternoon the path clears and we encounter the first close views of the towering cliffs of Mt. Meru and the stunning ash cone. Miriakampa Hut, situated in idyllic grassy glade, is reached in time to enjoy the afternoon sun and beautiful views over the surrounding plains towards Mount Kilimanjaro.
From here we can go on an evening game walk in hopes of watching some wildlife at one of the watering holes in the crater.

itinerary.title: Miriakamba Hut to Saddle Hut
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:2-3 hours
Hiking Distance:4 km
Starting Altitude:2516m
Final Altitude:3570m
Environment: Heath
The track from Miriakampa Hut to the saddle below Little Meru is a steep sustained trek that tests your legs. Our track takes us through beautiful and lush montane forest and striking tree species such as hygenium abyssinica, nuxia congesta, podocarpus, and hypericum tevolutum with mosses and lichens adorning the ground and trees.
Passing the halfway point of Mgongo wa Tembo (Elephant Back Ridge) we pass through giant heather and moorland vegetation, home to common shrubs such as erica arbores, stoebe kilimandscharica and leonits nepatifolia.
Around midday we reach the alpine zone of Saddle Hut where we rest, set up our chairs and tables and enjoy a picnic lunch.
In the afternoon, trekkers, feeling energetic can make the short climb to the nearby summit of Little Meru (3820 m/ 12,533 ft) for superb views of Socialist Peak and the steep winding trail that awaits us the next morning. The round trip ascent of Little Meru takes 1-1.5 hours.
At these higher altitudes we encounter magnificent birdlife including the bearded vulture soaring high above us, white- naked raven, lammerger, stonechat, alpine swift and cliff chat found around camp.

itinerary.title: Saddle Hut to Summit to Miriakamba Hut-Momela gate –Arusha
itinerary.description:
Today’s Stats Hiking Time:4-5 hours ascent + 6-8 hours descent
Hiking Distance:5 km ascent + 15 km descent
Starting Altitude:2516m
Summit:4566m
Final Altitude:2516m
Environment: Alpine Desert
At around 3am we rise, put on all our warm clothes and enjoy a hot cup of tea or chocolate before setting out
on the trail. The first hour is a steep climb to Rhino Point (3800m/12,467ft), and then the path continues along a narrow but spectacular ridge of ash and rock to reach Cobra Point (4350m/14,272ft).
The summit is now within our reach and after an hour of climbing and light scrambling over rocks and boulders we look up to see the summit flag beckoning us onwards and upwards.
Arriving at the summit we are greeted with stunning views of the crater rim, the spectacular ash cone rising from the crater floor, Mount Kilimanjaro floating on the morning clouds just 70km away, and the Rift Valley in the distance.
After soaking up the magnificent vistas and celebrating our summit success we begin our descent where we may encounter the delicately-hoofed klipspringers bounding from rock to rock in the early morning light. The route back to Rhino Point, in the sharp morning light traverses a narrow ridge between the sloping outer wall of the crater and the sheer cliffs of the inner wall, is one of the most dramatic and exhilarating walks in Africa.

title: 4-Days Zanzibar beach tour exploration
overview:
Description of the tour

Zanzibar is an archipelago off the coast of East Africa, part of the United Republic of Tanzania, known for its idyllic beaches, rich history, and vibrant cultural mixes. It consists primarily of two main islands which are Unguja often simply referred to as “Zanzibar” and Pemba as well as numerous smaller islands. Unguja, the largest island, is where Zanzibar City and the historic Stone Town are located. A four-day tour to Zanzibar is a fantastic way to experience the island’s stunning beaches, rich cultural heritage, and unique natural beauty. Zanzibar captures the best of the island’s history, culture, and natural beauty, offering a blend of relaxation and exploration in one of the Indian Ocean’s most breathtaking destinations.

Highlights of the tour

  • Stone town city exploration
  • Prison island visit
  • Spice farm experience
  • Beach experience
  • Mnemba snorkeling

Located on the western coast of Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago, Stone Town offers a unique fusion of architecture, history, and vibrant cultural life that reflects its centuries-old role as a major trade center in the Indian Ocean. itinerary.title: Mnemba snorkelling
itinerary.description: Mnemba Atoll, located off the northeastern coast of Zanzibar, Tanzania, is renowned for its stunning snorkelling experiences. This small, private island is surrounded by crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral reefs, making it a popular destination for snorkelers and divers alike. The waters around Mnemba Atoll are teeming with marine life. Snorkelers can expect to see a variety of colourful fish, including parrotfish, clownfish, and angelfish, as well as sea turtles, dolphins, and even the occasional reef shark. In the morning after breakfast your guide will pick you up heading to Mnemba Atoll where you will spend the day to dive and snorkel in that beautiful Atoll. At noon the lunch will be provided where you will enjoy the most stunning sea food and fresh fruits or juice. Later in the evening you will jump in the boat heading to your accommodation centre for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Spice farm tour and airport transfer
itinerary.description: After having a strong breakfast, you guide will pick you up to start a tour heading to spice farm. A spice farm tour in Zanzibar is a unique, immersive experience that delves into the island’s rich history as a spice hub and offers a sensory exploration of its agricultural treasures. Known as the "Spice Island," Zanzibar has a tropical climate ideal for cultivating a variety of spices such as cloves, cinnamon, black pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, and vanilla. These spices, which once drove Zanzibar’s economy and established its historical significance on the trade routes, remain an integral part of the island’s identity and local culture. Later after finish the spice tour you have a chance to visit different souvenirs shop and your guide will drop off at the airport or any other place you want.

title: Materuni Waterfalls
overview:
Driving Time from Moshi: 45 minutes
Altitude: 1,600m above sea level
Hiking Time: 30 minutes
Coffee Tour Duration: 1 hour
Location: Near Moshi Town

Materuni Waterfall is the highest and most impressive waterfall at the foothills of Mt. Kilimanjaro, located at latitude -3.25025° (3° 15′ 1″ S) and longitude 37.40007° (37° 24′ 0″ E).

Upon arrival, you will complete the necessary formalities before embarking on a scenic 40-minute hike down to the village and waterfall. The trail takes you through rolling hills and valleys covered in lush tropical rainforests, and coffee, banana, and avocado farms, locally known as shambas. Your guide will provide insights into the flora, fauna, and local farming practices.

Once you reach the waterfall, you can take in its breathtaking beauty and enjoy a refreshing swim in the cool, clear waters, so don’t forget to bring your swimming gear.

After the waterfall visit, you’ll experience an authentic coffee tour, where you will learn about the entire coffee production process from cultivation and harvesting to roasting and brewing done the traditional Chagga way. You’ll even get to roast and prepare your cup of freshly brewed coffee.

To complete your experience, you’ll enjoy a delicious traditional meal featuring a variety of local dishes and fresh seasonal fruits. This will give you a true taste of the region’s culture before departing the village.

On a clear day, you’ll also be rewarded with stunning views of Kibo Peak and Moshi town during the hike. Please note that the trek to the waterfall can be physically demanding, so sturdy hiking boots are highly recommended.

title: Lake Chala Day Tour
overview:
Lake Chala Safari is a private game reserve located on the western slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro, near the Kenya-Tanzania border. It is approximately a 2.5-hour drive from Moshi and 8 km from Taveta. The reserve is named after Lake Chala, a unique caldera lake, also known as Dschalla, with a depth of over 3,000 meters making it one of Africa’s deepest inland water bodies.

Upon arrival, our guide will take you to various viewpoints where you can explore the region’s diverse flora and fauna. You will then descend towards the lakeshore, passing through lush green vegetation with breathtaking views of the deep blue lake ahead. The lake’s crystal clear waters are home to a variety of fish, though swimming is not highly recommended.

The walk around the lake offers stunning scenery but can be a bit challenging. Along the way, you may encounter wildlife such as lizards, baboons, monkeys, and even snakes.

After your tour, you can unwind at the camp’s scenic bar overlooking the lake, where you can enjoy a refreshing drink while taking in the tranquil surroundings.

title: Chemka Hot Spring Tour
overview:
We will pick you up from your hotel in Moshi early in the morning for a one-hour drive to Kikuletwa Chemka Hot Springs, a stunning geothermal oasis. The crystal-clear waters, heated naturally from underground springs, create a refreshing and relaxing environment. Despite its name, the water is warm rather than hot, and some areas reach depths of up to 10 meters, allowing for incredible visibility. A swimsuit is essential for this experience.

After enjoying your swim, we will take you to a nearby restaurant for a delicious hot lunch and provide you with bottled water. Following lunch, you will have plenty of time to relax and take another dip in the springs. Keep an eye out for local wildlife, including vervet monkeys, which often visit the area.

By late afternoon, we will return to Moshi, leaving you refreshed and rejuvenated after this unforgettable experience at Chemka Hot Springs.

itinerary.description:
Departure from Arusha after breakfast and drive approximately 3.5 hours to Ngorongoro. You will arrive in time for lunch at your hotel/lodge and have ample time in the afternoon to relax and enjoy the great view of the crater floor from the crater rim where your lodge camp is situated.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, you will drive for approximately 30 minutes to the crater floor. Upon arrival, you will be amazed by the concentration and sheer number and diversity of animals and bird life! Seated or standing in your safari vehicle, the game viewing opportunities will be endless...
The Ngorongoro Crater is a breathtakingly beautiful setting and the best place in East Africa to see the Big Five. On the crater floor you can expect to see herds of zebra, wildebeest, Thomson’s gazelle, Grant’s gazelle, topi and many more. Sightings of predators such as lion, hyena, jackal and bat-eared fox regularly occur here as well. Although cheetah and leopard are a little more scarce in this park, they can still be spotted with a little luck.  Ngorongoro Crater is also one of a handful of places in Africa where you have a very good chance of seeing rhino, though usually from a distance. Bird species are also numerous and varied here.
After your wonderful safari day, you will be driven back to your lodge for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro - Serengeti National Park
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast you will continue your journey, passing through the Ngorongoro Conservation Area on the way to Serengeti National Park. Here, the sublime landscapes are home to the Maasai herdsmen who live alongside the area's abundant wildlife. You will stop along the way at a Masai Boma (village) and meet some of the people who live there. Your drive will then continue through the rolling landscapes upon which you may spot Grant’s and Thomson’s gazelles, giraffes, wildebeest, zebra, buffalo and more.
You will arrive at Serengeti National Park's Nabi Gate around lunchtime. Here you will eat before embarking on your first game drive that will take you to the Seronera region in central Serengeti. Seronera is one of the richest wildlife habitats in the park as the Seronera River provides a valuable water source to the area, therefore attracting an abundance of wildlife.
After your wonderful afternoon exploring East Africa's most famous park, we will head to your lodge/tented camp for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Serengeti National Park
itinerary.description:
After breakfast you will have a full day to explore Serengeti with both morning and afternoon game drives.
The Serengeti National Park is the jewel in the crown of Tanzania’s game parks and offers arguably the best game viewing in Africa. The setting is perfect – a sea of endless plains that stretches to the horizon, dotted with the acacia trees and termite mounds. Serengeti is home to huge herds of wildebeest that every year make the mass migration north, through crocodile infested rivers, in a frenzied mixture of mating and galloping that is driven by instinct. Prides of lion rule here, as their hungry gazes sweep the savannah for a chance to attack one of the thousands of eland, impala and gazelle. Solitary leopards lie high in the branches of the acacia tree while herds of elephants roam at will. This is the Africa that you have always dreamed about.
After another amazing day of explorations, you will return to your lodge/tented camp for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Pick up from the Airport to Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description:
Pick up at Arusha Airport and transfer to Tarangire National Park for Game Drive. You will drive for approximately 2.5 hrs to Tarangire National Park. Tarangire is a lovely, quiet park in Northern Tanzania. It is most famous for its elephant migration, birding and authentic safari atmosphere.
 Every year during the dry season from June to November, the wildlife migrate through the park allowing for a very large number of different species to be seen here. As most of this part of the country is dry, the Tarangire River remains the only source of water and consequently attracts large numbers of wildebeests, elephants, gazelles, zebras, hartebeest, buffaloes and various predators such as lions and cheetahs that come to drink and graze around the river banks. Large swathes of Tarangire remain almost untouched, especially in the southern region of the park.  With game-viewing that is exceptional in the dry season, this Tanzanian safari park is a small gem on the Northern safari circuit, especially if you love elephants! After game drive you will drive to Karatu town for Dinner and Overnight at Eileens Tree Inn (Full Board)

itinerary.title: Karatu - Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description:
After breakfast 08:00am, we will start our journey to Ngorongoro Crater it is closer 15 minutes’ drive from the hotel to the gate and 45 minutes to reach top of crater. After the registration formalities at the gate, we drive 45 minutes and you will you descend in 600 meters deep a 20kms across, and 300 sq kms caldera which is a breathtaking experience for the game drive. This magnificent crater is one of the most densely crowded African wildlife areas in the world and is home to an estimated 30,000 animals including some of Tanzania’s last remaining Black Rhino. Supported by a year-round water supply and fodder, the Ngorongoro crater support a vast variety of animals, which include herds of Wildebeest, Zebra, Buffalo, Eland, Warthog, Hippo, and giant African Elephants. Another uniqueness of the crater is its huge population of predators, which include Lions, Hyenas, Jackals, Cheetahs and the ever-elusive Leopard. In the afternoon, you will enjoy your picnic lunch at the Hippo pool. Later, you will continue with afternoon game drive for 2-3hours then after you will ascend the crater.
 After an amazing game drive you will begin your journey back to Arusha in the late afternoon. You will be dropped off at your hotel in Arusha or at Arusha Airport or Kilimanjaro International Airport, depending on what your plans are for the remainder of your stay in Tanzania.

itinerary.title: Arusha to Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: Today you will be picked up at your hotel after breakfast and hit the road in direction of Tarangire National Park. Tarangire is a lovely, quiet park in Northern Tanzania. It is most famous for its elephant migration, birding and authentic safari atmosphere. Every year during the dry season from June to November, the wildlife migrates through the park allowing for a very large number of different species to be seen here. As most of this part of the country is dry, the Tarangire River remains the only source of water and consequently attracts large numbers of wildebeests, elephants, gazelles, zebras, hartebeest, buffaloes and various predators such as lions and cheetahs that come to drink and graze around the river banks. Large swathes of Tarangire remain almost untouched, especially in the southern region of the park. With game-viewing that is exceptional in the dry season, this Tanzanian safari park is a small gem on the Northern safari circuit, especially if you love elephants! During the 2-hour guided tour, led by an English-speaking staff member, you'll hear poignant stories about the animals' backgrounds and might assist in feeding them, with species like vervet and blue monkeys, baboons, smaller antelopes, a cheetah, and various bird species. You will start your adventure via back road in an off beaten track. During the ride you will enjoy the wonderful scenery and authentic Tanzanian life as it unfolds along the road. On arrival at Chemka Hot Springs you will have an opportunity to refresh yourself in an oasis of geothermal warmth that bubbles up from underground after a long adventure. Your guide will give detailed descriptions of what each plant is used for, and not all are for food. title: Oldoinyo Lengai Mountain Trek
overview:
Two days One Night Oldoinyo Lengai and Lake Natron Tour

Overview

Ol Doinyo Lengai Mountain (2890 metres) is located some 240 kilometres to the Northwest of Arusha town, along the western escarpment of the Great East African Rift Valley, overlooking Lake Natron on the border with Kenya. Ol Doinyo Lengai, or Mountain of God in Maasai, is the only active volcano in Tanzania. Lake Natron which is lying at the base on the Mountain is said to be the only breeding area for the endangered Lesser Flamingoes that live in the Great Rift Valley and it is believed to be the world’s most important breeding site for the Lesser Flamingoes, accounting for 75 per cent of the global population. You can climb Ol Doinyo Lengai for six hours.

Day 01: Arusha Town to Lake Natron

Our driver will pick you up at your hotel in Arusha in the morning and drive you to Lake Natron. The drive is fairly long and you will reach at the campsite in the afternoon around 1pm. You will have your lunch at the picnic site. The scenery on the way is picturesque and you will have an opportunity to see some African wildlife on the way and the Maasai grazing cattle along Zebra and Wildebeest. After your after lunch, you will visit Ngaresero waterfall. After waterfalls you will visit the Lake Natron and later return at the campsite for overnight.

Day 02: Climbing Oldoinyo Lengai Mountain

At 1:00 a.m. driver and your guide will take you to the foot of Ol Doinyo Lengai volcano for the start of your climb. The footing on the slopes of the volcano can be treacherous, especially in the dark, so follow your guide. The trek is strenuous and it takes between 7 and 12 hours depending on your fitness and resultant pace. The gradient is steep, so it is best to make a short stop with every 100m or so of altitude gained in order to get acclimatized. At the edge of the crater the altitude is 2,960 m. The descent is easier and you may be tempted to move faster. This is, however, the time when most injuries happen, so mind your step! It is also advisable to change your fleece for a sun hat after dawn in order to avoid heatstroke. Our driver will be awaiting you as you return to the foot of the mountain with cold drinks. Later you will start your journey to Arusha or Mto wa mbu and Karatu if going to Safari.

A 8-day trek on the Lemosho Route offers an incredible opportunity to summit one of the world’s most beautiful and unique mountains while being surrounded by pristine nature. Our professional guides and experienced crew will ensure your safety and comfort throughout the journey, managing every step of your trek with expertise—so there’s no need for fear or regrets.

The Lemosho Route is ideal for acclimatization, allowing climbers to ascend to higher altitudes during the day while sleeping at lower elevations overnight. The route can be completed in 7 or 8 days, but we highly recommend the 8-day itinerary to allow for better acclimatization and increase the chances of a successful summit.

itinerary.title: Climbing from Shira Camp 2 to Barranco Camp
itinerary.description:
After an early morning breakfast, you will leave the moorland environment and enter a semi-desert, rocky landscape. The trek eastward takes approximately five hours, leading you to the impressive Lava Tower at 4,630 meters. Along the way, you will take short breaks and enjoy snacks to maintain energy.
 After reaching Lava Tower, the descent begins toward Barranco Camp at 3,950 meters. This route follows the principle of "climb high, sleep low," which helps your body acclimate to the high altitude.
 Barranco Camp is nestled in a scenic valley below the Breach and the towering Great Barranco Wall. As the day ends, you can relax and enjoy dinner while watching the stunning sunset over Kilimanjaro.
 Hiking Time: 6 to 7 hoursElevation: 3840m / 12600 ft to 3976m /130044 ftDistance: 8 km (5 miles)

itinerary.title: Climbing from Barranco Camp to Karanga Valley Camp
itinerary.description:
This is a short trekking day designed for acclimatization. After an early breakfast, you will begin the climb up the Great Barranco Wall. Although it may appear challenging at first, hikers often find this Class 2 climb easier than expected.
 At the top of the wall, you will be rewarded with breathtaking views of Heim Glacier and the experience of trekking above the clouds. The trail then winds through a series of ascents and descents in the Karanga Valley before reaching Karanga Camp at 3,950 meters.
 Upon arrival, you will have time to rest, enjoy dinner, and freshen up in preparation for the next day's climb to Barafu Camp.
 Distance: 5 km / 3 milesTime: 4 to 5 hoursElevation: 3,976 m / 13,044 ft to 3,995 m / 13,106 ftZone: High Alpine Zone

itinerary.title: Karanga Valley to Barafu Camp
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, you will begin your ascent toward Barafu Camp. The trail merges with the Mweka Route, which will be used for descent after the summit. As you continue hiking, you will reach Barafu Hut, the final camp before the summit attempt.
 Barafu Camp, situated at 4,550 meters, marks the last water stop for porters, as there is no accessible water beyond this point. The name "Barafu" means "ice" in Swahili, reflecting the camp’s cold, rocky, and exposed environment. Strong winds and rugged terrain make this site a challenging but essential resting point before the summit push.
 An early dinner will be served to allow time for rest before the midnight summit attempt. Your guide will provide a detailed briefing on how to prepare for the climb to Uhuru Peak.
 Elevation: 13,106 ft to 15,331 ftDistance: 4 km / 2 milesHiking Time: 4 to 5 hoursHabitat: Alpine Desert

itinerary.title: Climbing to Uhuru Peak
itinerary.description:
Your guide will wake you around 11:30 PM for a light snack of tea and biscuits before beginning the summit attempt. Moving at a slow and steady pace ("pole-pole"), you will ascend towards Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa at 5,895 meters.
 The trail heads northwest, taking you over rocky terrain and loose scree. Many hikers find this stretch to be the most physically and mentally demanding part of the climb. After about six hours of trekking, you will reach Stella Point at 5,685 meters, situated on the crater rim. Here, you will witness a breathtaking sunrise over the vast landscape.
 From Stella Point, the final push to Uhuru Peak takes approximately two more hours along a snow-covered path. Reaching the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro is a once-in-a-lifetime achievement. You will have a short time at the peak to take photographs and soak in the incredible views before beginning the descent.
 Descending back to Barafu Camp takes a few hours, where you will rest and enjoy a hot lunch in the sun. After eating, the journey continues down the Mweka Trail, leading through rocky terrain, moorland, and into the rainforest. The day concludes at Mweka Camp (3,100 meters), where you will have dinner and a well-earned rest. Expect mist and occasional rain, as the camp is nestled in the upper rainforest zone.
 Summit Ascent: Barafu Camp to Uhuru PeakElevation: 15,331 ft to 19,341 ftDistance: 5 km / 3 milesHiking Time: 7 to 8 hoursHabitat: Arctic
 Descent: Uhuru Peak to Mweka CampElevation: 19,341 ft to 10,065 ftDistance: 12 km / 7 milesHiking Time: 4 to 6 hoursHabitat: Rainforest

itinerary.title: Descend to Mweka Gate
itinerary.description:
After a well-earned breakfast, it’s time to bid farewell to Mount Kilimanjaro. Before descending, your trekking team will hold a celebratory gathering filled with singing and dancing to mark the completion of your journey. This is also the moment to express your gratitude by presenting tips to your guides, assistant guides, chefs, and porters.
 Following the celebration, you will begin your final descent, a three-hour trek down to Mweka Gate. Upon arrival, all hikers are required to sign in with the National Park authorities to receive their certificates of achievement. Those who reached Stella Point (5,685 meters) will receive a green certificate, while those who reached Uhuru Peak (5,895 meters) will be awarded a gold certificate.
 After receiving your certificate, you will continue descending for another hour (approximately 3 kilometers) through the lush rainforest to Mweka Village. From there, a vehicle will be waiting to transfer you back to your hotel in Moshi, where you can relax and celebrate your incredible accomplishment.
 Elevation: 10,065 ft to 5,380 ftDistance: 10 km / 6 milesHiking Time: 3 to 4 hoursHabitat: Rainforest

title: 1-Day Kilimanjaro Trekking to Mandara Hut
overview:
Overview

The Mount Kilimanjaro Day tour is perfect for those who want to get the taste of the Kilimanjaro Mountain but have limited time while in Moshi or Arusha town. Experience incredible scenery and breathtaking landscapes, and keep your eyes peeled for monkeys and native bird species. This tour is a perfect way to discover the natural beauty of Mount Kilimanjaro.

Tour description

After breakfast, our driver-guide will pick you up from your hotel and drive to Kilimanjaro National Park Marangu Gate, 1860 m. The drive will take approximately 1 hour from Moshi. After registration, you will head directly into the park, where you will start your trekking adventure. Alongside the impressive vegetation, you will have the chance to catch a glimpse of black and white colobus monkeys, blue monkeys, and various bird species. Our knowledgeable English-speaking guide will inform you about Mount Kilimanjaro and will explain the different species of plants and animals available in the park. Depending on your fitness level, after 3-4 hours of walking, you will arrive at Mandara Hut, located at 9,000 feet (2,743 meters) above sea level, where a delicious picnic lunch will be served over there.

After lunch, you will trek further for about 15 minutes to the Maundi crater, another breathtakingly beautiful location on Kilimanjaro. You will be able to view the peak of his majesty Kilimanjaro on less cloudy days. After enjoying the astounding landscapes, you will start descending back for 2 hours to Marangu Gate. Our driver guide will drive you from the gate to your hotel. On your return journey, you can enjoy the sunset and your memories of the day.

And Ngurdoto Crater is one of the most dazzling anywhere in Tanzania; it’s smaller than Ngorongoro but otherwise is just as impressive.

title: 1-Day to Lake Manyara National park
overview: Almost everyone who visits Lake Manyara National Park falls in love with this unique park. Lake Manyara is most famous for being one of the few parks in Africa where its lions climb trees. It’s not unusual to look up into the branches of Lake Manyara’s forest canopy and find yourself face-to-face with a lion (or even an entire pride). Large populations of elephants and olive baboons are further highlights, while the backdrop to all wildlife sightings here is the dramatic Rift Valley escarpment, which rises over the park’s western boundary, or pretty Lake Manyara, which dominates the east.

itinerary.title: Day plan
itinerary.description: We will drive you to Lake Manyara National Park. A park that supports one of the highest biomass densities of large mammals in the world. Famous for the tree-climbing lions, the soda ash lake, and its flamingos, it displays the breathtaking scenery of the Rift Valley. The number of bird species it houses, including flamingos, pelicans, cormorants, and a few hundred other species, makes it appear like a paradise for ornithologists. Next to a great variety of birds, the “Big Game” can also be seen. With a bit of luck, you might see elephants in the wooded regions, and with even more fortune, the tree-climbing lions. Indeed, it was thought for a long time that Lake Manyara National Park is the only place where lions can be found with this atypical behavior of climbing trees. Baboons and velvet monkeys are also found among the forested areas, and in the more open spaces, giraffes nibble at the fresh leaves while the various types of antelopes common to the region browse for tasty shoots.

title: 1-Day to Ngorongoro Crater Tour
overview: The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Ngorongoro District, 180 km (110 mi) west of Arusha City in the Arusha Region, within the Crater Highlands geological area of northern Tanzania. The area is named after Ngorongoro Crater, a large volcanic caldera within the area. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority administers the conservation area, an arm of the Tanzanian government, and its boundaries follow the boundary of the Ngorongoro District in the Arusha Region. The western portion of the park abuts the Serengeti National Park, and the area comprising the two parks and Kenya’s Maasai Mara game reserve is home to Great Migration, a massive annual migration of millions of wildebeest, zebras, gazelles, and other animals. The conservation area also contains Olduvai Gorge, one of the most important paleoanthropological sites in the world.

title: 1-Day Tarangire National Park Exploration
overview: Tarangire National Park contains a variety of wildlife, both big and small. The park is popular for the high elephant population; you may see them roaming around in the bush searching for food and relaxation. During the dry season, see them heading to the river just enjoying the pure drinks and cooling themselves from the hot sun during the daytime. The park also contains over 500 bird species and a beautiful landscape nourished with baobab trees that stand as towers in the savannah land. These ancient baobab trees play a vital role in ecosystems used as habitat for bees, birds, and bats. Also, they have beautiful fruits and store water, hence providing support during the dry season.

title: 1-Day Mkomazi National Park Exploration
overview: Experience wild Africa in Mkomazi National Park. The wildlife you’ll see here might include elephants that come in across the border from Kenya, as well as oryx, eland, kudu, and Coke’s hartebeest. You might even see the long-necked gerenuk. Birdlife is another highlight, and this is a real hot spot for bird-watchers, drawn here by over 400 different kinds of birds. But most people also love the classic safari landscapes—the views of Mt. Kilimanjaro, the baobab and acacia trees, the low rocky hills, and the wild bushland. And best of all, you might just have this place all to yourself.
